acceptance_criteria.criterion: Seed workforce.view, workforce.manage, and workforce.publish into org_role_permissions for the eight organization-wide roles so live routes stop returning a plausible zero.
evidence: A REAL TWO-LAYER TEST, not a matrix read. Layer 1 is executed by importing the module the running application imports — lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts, through supabase/tests/db016_capability_gate_probe.mjs — and answering what resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilities returns for the matrix row the database actually holds, with exactly the inputs loadCapabilities supplies (lib/auth/admin-context.ts:237-242) and with no target and no department authority, because has_perm has no target argument and that is the only projection the two layers can be compared on. Layer 2 is the chain's own has_perm, called as a real membership. The two are diffed over all 36 (role, workforce permission) pairs: 0 disagreements after, 13 before. BOTH SIDES MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY: the vitest test runs the real resolver over the harness's exported database answers, and the harness runs its own comparison independently of any test runner, so one instrument being wrong cannot make both green. FOUR THINGS make this more than a matrix read: (1) the negative control, where the same comparator fed a matrix with no workforce grant REPORTS all 3 disagreements, so the zero after is a measurement rather than an instrument that always says zero; (2) the BEFORE measurement over the before-matrix and the before-state has_perm answers captured in stage 1, which is 13 disagreements — the comparator is shown to have found this defect before it is trusted with its absence; (3) the gate-implies-rows assertion, run against REAL authenticated sessions through the chain's own staff_members_scoped_read, so 'the gate admitted them' and 'the rows came back' are two different measurements; (4) the no-cross-tenant assertion for all twelve roles, because widening a role matrix is the one way this migration could turn a zero into a disclosure. THE RESIDUAL IS MEASURED AND REPORTED, NOT ABSORBED: the superset pairs across the whole 42-capability catalog are 206 after this migration (owner=37 admin=35 tour_manager=26 production=24 production_manager=24 department_manager=11 finance=13 finance_manager=14 ticketing=7 ticketing_manager=7 viewer=9 worker=0), of which the workforce family's share is exactly 0. CP-110 as a general rule is therefore satisfied for the workforce family only, and the test says so in its name and in its output rather than implying otherwise.
Preserved v1 criterion metadata: {"id":3,"text":"The split-brain is proven closed by test: a caller passing the application capability gate can read the rows RLS governs","met":true}

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Seed workforce.view, workforce.manage, and workforce.publish into org_role_permissions for the eight organization-wide roles so live routes stop returning a plausible zero.
evidence: PROVEN TWO WAYS, and the second is the one that matters. (1) STRUCTURALLY: the write is `insert ... on conflict (role) do update set perms = <sorted de-duplicated union of the existing row and the declared slice>`, so there is no code path through which a pre-existing permission can leave the array. (2) AS A MEASUREMENT OF THE TARGET'S REAL PRE-STATE: the migration snapshots the whole matrix as JSONb inside the same transaction, writes, and then asserts that every permission every role held before is still present, raising with the role and the permission named. That is only expressible with the snapshot and the write in one transaction, which is why the whole file is one DO block; stated in the header. The harness prints the per-role before/after diff — removed:[…] added:[…] for all twelve roles, removed empty every time — and __tests__/admin/db016-capability-matrix-agreement.test.ts independently diffs the harness's exported before/after matrices and prints the same diff. `staff.manage` is the load-bearing case because it is the pre-existing organization-administrator grant DB-013 already recorded as retained: owner and admin both still carry it, asserted in the migration, the postflight and the vitest test. PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: a tampered copy that strips staff.manage from the union is REJECTED with 'DB-016 is additive and refuses to remove a granted permission; these would be REMOVED: admin: staff.manage, owner: staff.manage, production: staff.manage, tour_manager: staff.manage', and the matrix is left byte-identical.
Preserved v1 criterion metadata: {"id":4,"text":"No previously granted permission is removed from any role","met":true}

FOUR REAL DEFECTS IN THIS LANE'S OWN NEW CODE, all found by the harness and all recorded because they are the reusable part. (a) The migration referenced the target table in an `insert ... select` SELECT list; PostgreSQL does not put the target in scope there, SQLSTATE 42P01, and the first apply aborted. The union moved into the ON CONFLICT clause, which is the correct form. (b) The union omitted DISTINCT, so a permission the target already held was kept twice; the migration's own exact-membership assertion correctly refused and the SECOND apply aborted, which is what made the non-idempotence visible. (c) The harness's expected_wf returned a comma-separated list while the membership test was a space-separated pattern match, so the harness reported 'has_perm does not agree with CP-102' for a matrix that agreed exactly — a false negative produced by the test, not by the migration, and the most dangerous shape an instrument can have. (d) The contract postflight used `'x' <> any (arr)` as the negation of `'x' = any (arr)`; it is not, it is true whenever x differs from ANY element, so the summary read `f` on a healthy target and two check blocks emitted rows unconditionally. All four fixed, all four recorded.
